interpretation_rules: Position weight is a common multiplicative factor within QB and therefore cannot by itself explain within-QB rank spacing.
A structural audit may identify compression or discontinuities but cannot select a new QB scale or curve.
Weeks 1-3 realized outcomes are early descriptive evidence only; they cannot authorize a model change.
Production V2 Phase 1 is an uncalibrated transparent benchmark, not a validated replacement.
No named QB may be manually raised or lowered from this audit.
Any follow-up model change requires a separately preregistered calibration/validation study.
primary_questions: Does the live QB board reproduce the exact deployed formula with no hidden QB-only adjustment?
How much of within-QB value spacing comes from production multiplier versus age multiplier?
Is the upper QB tier mechanically compressed, and if so what component creates the compression?
Do role-floor, elite-floor, no-history, clamp, or missing-source semantics create discontinuities?
Does the transparent Production V2 benchmark materially reorder the QB cohort or mostly preserve the current ordering?
Does legacy production-multiplier lineage show unusual QB drift relative to other positions?
What do the already-frozen Weeks 1-3 prospective diagnostics say about current QB value ordering, while respecting that Weeks 1-3 are collection-only?
scope: All current PLAYER_DB quarterbacks in the deployed calculator.
